rows.question: Please generate a summary of the closing balances at the end of each month for each customer transactions, show the monthly changes and monthly cumulative bank account balances. Ensure that even if a customer has no account activity in a given month, the balance for that month is still included in the output.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH valid_txn AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(substr(txn_date,1,10)) AS txn_date,
    LOWER(txn_type) AS txn_type,
    txn_amount
  FROM customer_transactions
  WHERE txn_date IS NOT NULL
    AND length(txn_date) >= 10
    AND substr(txn_date,1,10) GLOB '[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]'
), 
txn_months AS (
  -- aggregate monthly net change per customer (deposit positive, others negative)
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    strftime('%Y-%m', txn_date) AS month,
    SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE -txn_amount END) AS month_net
  FROM valid_txn
  GROUP BY customer_id, month
),
cust_ranges AS (
  -- determine first and last month per customer
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    MIN(strftime('%Y-%m', txn_date)) AS first_month,
    MAX(strftime('%Y-%m', txn_date)) AS last_month
  FROM valid_txn
  GROUP BY customer_id
),
months AS (
  -- generate a calendar of months per customer between first and last month
  SELECT
    c.customer_id,
    strftime('%Y-%m', date(first_month || '-01', '+' || (n.n) || ' months')) AS month
  FROM cust_ranges c,
       (
         SELECT 0 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4
         UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9
         UNION ALL SELECT 10 UNION ALL SELECT 11 UNION ALL SELECT 12 UNION ALL SELECT 13 UNION ALL SELECT 14
         UNION ALL SELECT 15 UNION ALL SELECT 16 UNION ALL SELECT 17 UNION ALL SELECT 18 UNION ALL SELECT 19
         UNION ALL SELECT 20 UNION ALL SELECT 21 UNION ALL SELECT 22 UNION ALL SELECT 23 UNION ALL SELECT 24
         UNION ALL SELECT 25 UNION ALL SELECT 26 UNION ALL SELECT 27 UNION ALL SELECT 28 UNION ALL SELECT 29
         UNION ALL SELECT 30 UNION ALL SELECT 31 UNION ALL SELECT 32 UNION ALL SELECT 33 UNION ALL SELECT 34
         UNION ALL SELECT 35 UNION ALL SELECT 36
       ) n
  WHERE date(first_month || '-01', '+' || n.n || ' months') <= date(last_month || '-01')
),
months_with_net AS (
  -- left join aggregated nets to calendar months, default 0 for months with no txns
  SELECT
    m.customer_id,
    m.month,
    IFNULL(t.month_net, 0) AS month_net
  FROM months m
  LEFT JOIN txn_months t
    ON m.customer_id = t.customer_id AND m.month = t.month
),
ordered AS (
  -- assign row numbers per customer ordered by month to enable cumulative sum
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    month,
    month_net,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month) AS rn
  FROM months_with_net
),
cumulative AS (
  -- compute cumulative closing balance per month via correlated subquery summing month_net up to current month
  SELECT
    o.customer_id,
    o.month,
    o.month_net,
    (SELECT SUM(month_net) FROM ordered o2
     WHERE o2.customer_id = o.customer_id AND o2.rn <= o.rn) AS closing_balance
  FROM ordered o
)
SELECT
  customer_id,
  month,
  closing_balance AS closing_balance,
  closing_balance - LAG(closing_balance,1,0) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month) AS monthly_change,
  closing_balance AS cumulative_balance
FROM cumulative
ORDER BY customer_id ASC, month ASC

rows.question: For each customer and each month of 2020, first calculate the month-end balance by adding all deposit amounts and subtracting all withdrawal amounts that occurred during that specific month. Then determine which month in 2020 has the highest count of customers with a positive month-end balance and which month has the lowest count. For each of these two months, compute the average month-end balance across all customers and provide the difference between these two averages

WITH customer_transaction_rows_2020_normalized AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    txn_date,
    CAST(strftime('%Y', txn_date) AS INTEGER) AS txn_year,
    CAST(strftime('%m', txn_date) AS INTEGER) AS txn_month,
    txn_type,
    txn_amount,
    CASE
      WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount
      WHEN txn_type = 'withdrawal' THEN -txn_amount
      ELSE txn_amount
    END AS signed_amount
  FROM customer_transactions
),
all_customers_population AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id
  FROM customer_transactions
),
customer_monthly_balance_agg AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    txn_year AS calendar_year,
    txn_month AS calendar_month,
    SUM(signed_amount) AS month_balance
  FROM customer_transaction_rows_2020_normalized
  WHERE CAST(strftime('%Y', txn_date) AS INTEGER) = 2020
  GROUP BY
    customer_id,
    txn_year,
    txn_month
),
monthly_stats AS (
  SELECT
    printf('%04d-%02d', m.calendar_year, m.calendar_month) AS month_id,
    m.calendar_year,
    m.calendar_month,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE COALESCE(mb.month_balance, 0) > 0) AS positive_count,
    AVG(COALESCE(mb.month_balance, 0)) AS avg_balance
  FROM
    (
      SELECT 2020 AS calendar_year, 1 AS calendar_month UNION ALL
      SELECT 2020,2 UNION ALL SELECT 2020,3 UNION ALL SELECT 2020,4 UNION ALL
      SELECT 2020,5 UNION ALL SELECT 2020,6 UNION ALL SELECT 2020,7 UNION ALL
      SELECT 2020,8 UNION ALL SELECT 2020,9 UNION ALL SELECT 2020,10 UNION ALL
      SELECT 2020,11 UNION ALL SELECT 2020,12
    ) AS m
    CROSS JOIN all_customers_population AS c
    LEFT JOIN customer_monthly_balance_agg AS mb
      ON mb.customer_id = c.customer_id
      AND mb.calendar_year = m.calendar_year
      AND mb.calendar_month = m.calendar_month
  GROUP BY m.calendar_year, m.calendar_month
)
SELECT
  h.month_id AS highest_month,
  h.positive_count AS highest_month_positive_customer_count,
  h.avg_balance AS highest_month_avg_balance,
  l.month_id AS lowest_month,
  l.positive_count AS lowest_month_positive_customer_count,
  l.avg_balance AS lowest_month_avg_balance,
  (h.avg_balance - l.avg_balance) AS avg_difference
FROM
  (
    SELECT month_id, positive_count, avg_balance, calendar_year, calendar_month
    FROM monthly_stats
    ORDER BY positive_count DESC, calendar_year, calendar_month
    LIMIT 1
  ) AS h
  CROSS JOIN
  (
    SELECT month_id, positive_count, avg_balance, calendar_year, calendar_month
    FROM monthly_stats
    ORDER BY positive_count ASC, calendar_year, calendar_month
    LIMIT 1
  ) AS l

rows.question: For each customer, group all deposits and withdrawals by the first day of each month to obtain a monthly net amount, then calculate each month’s closing balance by cumulatively summing these monthly nets. Next, determine the most recent month’s growth rate by comparing its closing balance to the prior month’s balance, treating deposits as positive and withdrawals as negative, and if the previous month’s balance is zero, the growth rate should be the current month’s balance multiplied by 100. Finally, compute the percentage of customers whose most recent month shows a growth rate of more than 5%.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH customer_transactions_normalized AS (
SELECT
  customer_id,
  txn_date,
  txn_type,
  txn_amount,
  CASE
    WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount
    ELSE -txn_amount
  END AS signed_amount,
  substr(txn_date, 1, 7) || '-01' AS txn_month
FROM customer_transactions
),
customer_monthly_net_amounts AS (
SELECT
  customer_id,
  txn_month,
  SUM(signed_amount) AS monthly_net_amount
FROM
  customer_transactions_normalized
GROUP BY
  customer_id,
  txn_month
),
customer_monthly_closing_balance_running AS (
SELECT
  m.customer_id,
  m.txn_month,
  m.monthly_net_amount,
  SUM(m.monthly_net_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY m.customer_id ORDER BY m.txn_month ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS closing_balance
FROM customer_monthly_net_amounts m
)
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS total_customers_considered,
  SUM(CASE WHEN growth_rate > 0.05 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS customers_with_growth_gt_5pct,
  100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN growth_rate > 0.05 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) AS percentage_customers_with_growth_gt_5pct
FROM (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    recent_closing,
    COALESCE(prior_closing, 0.0) AS prior_closing,
    CASE
      WHEN COALESCE(prior_closing, 0.0) = 0.0 THEN recent_closing * 100.0
      ELSE (recent_closing - prior_closing) / prior_closing
    END AS growth_rate
  FROM (
    SELECT
      customer_id,
      closing_balance AS recent_closing,
      LAG(closing_balance) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY txn_month) AS prior_closing,
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY txn_month DESC) AS rn
    FROM customer_monthly_closing_balance_running
  ) recent_rows
  WHERE rn = 1
)

rows.question: For each month, calculate the total balance from all users for the previous month (measured as of the 1st of each month), replacing any negative balances with zero. Ensure that data from the first month is used only as a baseline for calculating previous total balance, and exclude it from the final output. Sort the results in ascending order by month.

WITH customer_transaction_rows AS (
SELECT
  customer_id,
  -- canonical ISO date YYYY-MM-DD: assume txn_date stored like '2020-01-21' or similar; try parsing common formats
  -- Use substrings to handle 'DD-MM-YYYY' or 'YYYY-MM-DD' or 'DD/MM/YYYY'
  CASE
    WHEN instr(txn_date, '-') = 3 AND instr(substr(txn_date,4), '-') = 3
      THEN -- format DD-MM-YYYY -> convert to YYYY-MM-DD
        substr(txn_date,7,4) || '-' || substr(txn_date,4,2) || '-' || substr(txn_date,1,2)
    WHEN instr(txn_date, '/') = 3 AND instr(substr(txn_date,4), '/') = 3
      THEN -- format DD/MM/YYYY -> convert to YYYY-MM-DD
        substr(txn_date,7,4) || '-' || substr(txn_date,4,2) || '-' || substr(txn_date,1,2)
    WHEN instr(txn_date, '-') = 5 AND instr(substr(txn_date,6), '-') = 0
      THEN -- format YYYY-MM-DD already
        txn_date
    ELSE
      txn_date
  END AS txn_date,
  txn_type,
  txn_amount
FROM customer_transactions
),
customer_monthly_balance_snapshot AS (
SELECT
  ctr.customer_id,
  strftime('%m-%Y', date(substr(ctr.txn_date,1,10))) AS month_year,
  SUM(ctr.txn_amount) OVER (
    PARTITION BY ctr.customer_id,
                 strftime('%Y-%m', date(substr(ctr.txn_date,1,10)))
    ORDER BY date(substr(ctr.txn_date,1,10)) ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
  ) AS balance
FROM customer_transaction_rows ctr
),
all_customers_monthly_nonnegative_total AS (
SELECT
  month_year,
  SUM(CASE WHEN balance < 0 THEN 0 ELSE balance END) AS total_balance
FROM
  customer_monthly_balance_snapshot
GROUP BY
  month_year
)
SELECT
  months.month_year,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN s.balance < 0 THEN 0 ELSE s.balance END), 0) AS total_balance
FROM
  (
    SELECT DISTINCT strftime('%Y-%m', txn_date) AS month_year
    FROM customer_transaction_rows

  -- exclude the dataset's first month
  JOIN (
    SELECT MIN(strftime('%Y-%m', txn_date)) AS first_month FROM customer_transaction_rows
  ) first_month_cte ON 1=1
  AND months.month_year > first_month_cte.first_month

    ON s.month_year = strftime('%Y-%m', date(months.month_year || '-01', '-1 month'))
GROUP BY
  months.month_year
ORDER BY
  months.month_year ASC

rows.question: For a bank database with customer transactions, calculate each customer's daily running balance (where deposits add to the balance and other transaction types subtract). For each customer and each day, compute the 30-day rolling average balance (only after having 30 days of data, and treating negative averages as zero). Then group these daily averages by month and find each customer's maximum 30-day average balance within each month. Sum these maximum values across all customers for each month. Consider the first month of each customer's transaction history as the baseline period and exclude it from the final results, presenting monthly totals of these summed maximum 30-day average balances.

WITH customer_daily_end_of_day_balance AS (
SELECT
  ct.customer_id,
  ct.txn_date,
  SUM(
    CASE
      WHEN ct.txn_type = 'deposit' THEN ct.txn_amount
      ELSE -ct.txn_amount
    END
  ) OVER (
    PARTITION BY ct.customer_id
    ORDER BY date(substr(ct.txn_date,1,10))
    ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
  ) AS end_of_day_balance
FROM customer_transactions ct
),
customer_30day_rolling_avg_nonneg_by_day AS (
SELECT
  d.customer_id,
  d.txn_date AS calendar_date,
  AVG(d.end_of_day_balance) OVER (
    PARTITION BY d.customer_id
    ORDER BY date(substr(d.txn_date,1,10)) 
    ROWS BETWEEN 29 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
  ) AS rolling_30d_avg,
  CASE
    WHEN AVG(d.end_of_day_balance) OVER (
      PARTITION BY d.customer_id
      ORDER BY date(substr(d.txn_date,1,10))
      ROWS BETWEEN 29 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) < 0 THEN 0
    ELSE AVG(d.end_of_day_balance) OVER (
      PARTITION BY d.customer_id
      ORDER BY date(substr(d.txn_date,1,10))
      ROWS BETWEEN 29 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    )
  END AS rolling_30d_avg_nonneg
FROM customer_daily_end_of_day_balance d
WHERE
  -- ensure at least 30 days of history by requiring the window to be full:
  (SELECT COUNT(1)
   FROM customer_daily_end_of_day_balance d2
   WHERE d2.customer_id = d.customer_id
     AND date(substr(d2.txn_date,1,10)) <= date(substr(d.txn_date,1,10))
     AND date(substr(d2.txn_date,1,10)) >= date(date(substr(d.txn_date,1,10)), '-29 days')
  ) >= 30
)
SELECT
  substr(r.calendar_date, 1, 7) AS month,
  SUM(per_cust.monthly_max) AS monthly_sum_max_30d_avg_balance
FROM customer_30day_rolling_avg_nonneg_by_day r
JOIN (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    substr(MIN(txn_date), 1, 7) AS baseline_month
  FROM customer_daily_end_of_day_balance
  GROUP BY customer_id
) b ON r.customer_id = b.customer_id
JOIN (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    substr(calendar_date,1,7) AS month,
    MAX(rolling_30d_avg_nonneg) AS monthly_max
  FROM customer_30day_rolling_avg_nonneg_by_day
  GROUP BY customer_id, substr(calendar_date,1,7)
) per_cust ON per_cust.customer_id = r.customer_id AND per_cust.month = substr(r.calendar_date,1,7)
WHERE substr(r.calendar_date,1,7) != b.baseline_month
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month ASC

Treat any negative daily balances as zero. Then, for each month, determine the highest daily balance each customer had during that month. Finally, for each month, sum these maximum daily balances across all customers to obtain a monthly total.

WITH customer_daily_transaction_sums AS (
SELECT
  customer_id,
  substr(txn_date, 1, 10) AS txn_date,
  SUM(txn_amount) AS daily_txn_sum
FROM customer_transactions
WHERE txn_date IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY customer_id, substr(txn_date, 1, 10)

customer_transaction_date_range AS (
SELECT
  customer_id,
  MIN(txn_date) AS min_txn_date,

FROM customer_transactions

calendar_days AS (

FROM (
  SELECT

    CAST(julianday(date(max(txn_date))) - julianday(date(min(txn_date))) AS INTEGER) AS span_days

  UNION ALL SELECT 60 UNION ALL SELECT 61 UNION ALL SELECT 62 UNION ALL SELECT 63 UNION ALL SELECT 64 UNION ALL SELECT 65 UNION ALL SELECT 66 UNION ALL SELECT 67 UNION ALL SELECT 68 UNION ALL SELECT 69
  UNION ALL SELECT 70 UNION ALL SELECT 71 UNION ALL SELECT 72 UNION ALL SELECT 73 UNION ALL SELECT 74 UNION ALL SELECT 75 UNION ALL SELECT 76 UNION ALL SELECT 77 UNION ALL SELECT 78 UNION ALL SELECT 79
  UNION ALL SELECT 80 UNION ALL SELECT 81 UNION ALL SELECT 82 UNION ALL SELECT 83 UNION ALL SELECT 84 UNION ALL SELECT 85 UNION ALL SELECT 86 UNION ALL SELECT 87 UNION ALL SELECT 88 UNION ALL SELECT 89
  UNION ALL SELECT 90 UNION ALL SELECT 91 UNION ALL SELECT 92 UNION ALL SELECT 93 UNION ALL SELECT 94 UNION ALL SELECT 95 UNION ALL SELECT 96 UNION ALL SELECT 97 UNION ALL SELECT 98 UNION ALL SELECT 99
) AS n
WHERE n.n <= bounds.span_days
)
SELECT
  cm.month_yyyy_mm AS month,
  SUM(cm.customer_month_max) AS monthly_total_max_balance
FROM (
  -- per-customer per-month max daily balance
  SELECT
    t.customer_id,
    substr(t.calendar_date,1,7) AS month_yyyy_mm,
    MAX(t.daily_balance) AS customer_month_max
  FROM (
    -- recursive build of daily balances per customer over their date range
    WITH RECURSIVE
    customer_days AS (
      SELECT
        c.customer_id,
        d.calendar_date
      FROM customer_transaction_date_range c
      JOIN calendar_days d
        ON d.calendar_date BETWEEN c.min_txn_date AND c.max_txn_date
    ),
    daily_txn AS (
      -- left join to get daily transaction sums (may be NULL -> 0)
      SELECT
        cd.customer_id,
        cd.calendar_date,
        COALESCE(s.daily_txn_sum, 0) AS daily_txn_sum
      FROM customer_days cd
      LEFT JOIN customer_daily_transaction_sums s
        ON s.customer_id = cd.customer_id
       AND s.txn_date = cd.calendar_date
    ),
    ordered_days AS (
      -- enumerated rows per customer to allow recursion by next date
      SELECT
        customer_id,
        calendar_date,
        daily_txn_sum,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY calendar_date) AS rn,
        COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id) AS cnt
      FROM daily_txn
    ),
    rec AS (
      -- seed: first day per customer uses previous balance 0
      SELECT
        o.customer_id,
        o.calendar_date,
        o.rn,
        o.cnt,
        MAX(0, o.daily_txn_sum) AS daily_balance
      FROM ordered_days o
      WHERE o.rn = 1

      UNION ALL

      -- recursive step: next day uses previous day's balance carried forward plus today's txn, floored at 0
      SELECT
        o.customer_id,
        o.calendar_date,
        o.rn,
        o.cnt,
        MAX(0, r.daily_balance + o.daily_txn_sum) AS daily_balance
      FROM rec r
      JOIN ordered_days o
        ON o.customer_id = r.customer_id
       AND o.rn = r.rn + 1
    )
    -- final per-day balances
    SELECT
      customer_id,
      calendar_date,
      daily_balance
    FROM rec
  ) t
  GROUP BY t.customer_id, substr(t.calendar_date,1,7)
) cm
GROUP BY cm.month_yyyy_mm
ORDER BY cm.month_yyyy_mm ASC

rows.question: Can you provide a breakdown of how many times each product was viewed, how many times they were added to the shopping cart, and how many times they were left in the cart without being purchased? Also, give me the count of actual purchases for each product. Ensure that products with a page id in (1, 2, 12, 13) are filtered out.

WITH shopping_cart_event_enriched AS (
SELECT
  e.visit_id,
  e.cookie_id,
  e.page_id,
  h.product_id,
  h.page_name,
  e.event_type,
  i.event_name,
  e.sequence_number,
  e.event_time
FROM shopping_cart_events e
JOIN shopping_cart_page_hierarchy h
  ON e.page_id = h.page_id
LEFT JOIN shopping_cart_event_identifier i
  ON e.event_type = i.event_type
WHERE e.page_id IS NOT NULL
),
product_catalog_from_pages AS (
SELECT
  page_hierarchy.product_id AS product_id,
  page_hierarchy.page_name AS canonical_product_name,
  page_hierarchy.page_id AS example_page_id
FROM shopping_cart_page_hierarchy AS page_hierarchy
WHERE page_hierarchy.product_id IS NOT NULL
),
product_event_counts_by_visit_cookie AS (
SELECT
  sce.product_id AS product_id,
  sce.visit_id AS visit_id,
  sce.cookie_id AS cookie_id,
  SUM(CASE WHEN sce.event_name = 'Page View' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS views_count,

GROUP BY
  sce.product_id,
  sce.visit_id,
  sce.cookie_id
)
SELECT
  p.product_id,
  COALESCE(p.canonical_product_name, CAST(p.product_id AS TEXT)) AS product_name,
  COALESCE(SUM(pe.views_count), 0) AS views_count,
  COALESCE(SUM(pe.add_to_cart_count), 0) AS add_to_cart_count,
  COALESCE(SUM(pe.purchases_count), 0) AS purchases_count,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN pe.add_to_cart_count > 0 AND COALESCE(pe.purchases_count,0) = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS abandonments_count
FROM product_catalog_from_pages p
LEFT JOIN product_event_counts_by_visit_cookie pe
  ON pe.product_id = p.product_id
GROUP BY
  p.product_id,
  p.canonical_product_name
ORDER BY
  views_count DESC

  interest_id,
  composition,
  index_value,
  composition / index_value AS composition_per_index

  SELECT

 AND imc.composition_per_index = mx.max_comp_per_index

  FROM batsman_scored bs

wickets_with_bowler_per_ball AS (

    ON w.match_id = be.match_id

top_batsmen AS (

rows.question: Find the IDs of players who scored the highest number of partnership runs for each match. The output should include the IDs of two players, each with their individual scores and the total partnership score. For each pair, the player with the higher individual score should be listed as player 1, and the player with the lower score as player 2. In cases where both players have the same score, the player with the higher ID should be player 1, and the player with the lower ID should be player 2. There can be multiple rows for a single match.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH deliveries_with_batsman_and_extras AS (
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.striker,
  b.non_striker,
  b.team_batting,
  b.team_bowling,
  COALESCE(bs.runs_scored, 0) AS runs_scored,
  COALESCE(er.extra_runs, 0) AS extra_runs,
  COALESCE(bs.runs_scored, 0) + COALESCE(er.extra_runs, 0) AS total_runs_on_ball
FROM ball_by_ball b
LEFT JOIN batsman_scored bs
  ON bs.match_id = b.match_id
  AND bs.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND bs.over_id = b.over_id
  AND bs.ball_id = b.ball_id
LEFT JOIN extra_runs er
  ON er.match_id = b.match_id
  AND er.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND er.over_id = b.over_id
  AND er.ball_id = b.ball_id
),
partnership_ball_ownership AS (
SELECT
  d.match_id,
  d.innings_no,
  d.over_id,
  d.ball_id,
  CASE
    WHEN d.striker <= d.non_striker THEN d.striker
    ELSE d.non_striker
  END AS batsman_a_id,
  CASE
    WHEN d.striker <= d.non_striker THEN d.non_striker
    ELSE d.striker
  END AS batsman_b_id,
  d.striker AS striker_id,
  d.non_striker AS non_striker_id,
  CASE WHEN d.striker = 
       CASE WHEN d.striker <= d.non_striker THEN d.striker ELSE d.non_striker END
    THEN COALESCE(d.runs_scored,0) ELSE 0 END AS batsman_a_runs_on_ball,
  CASE WHEN d.striker = 
       CASE WHEN d.striker <= d.non_striker THEN d.non_striker ELSE d.striker END
    THEN COALESCE(d.runs_scored,0) ELSE 0 END AS batsman_b_runs_on_ball,
  COALESCE(d.extra_runs,0) AS extra_runs_on_ball,
  COALESCE(d.total_runs_on_ball, COALESCE(d.runs_scored,0) + COALESCE(d.extra_runs,0)) AS total_runs_on_ball
FROM deliveries_with_batsman_and_extras d
),
partnerships_per_innings AS (
SELECT
  pbo.match_id,
  pbo.innings_no,
  -- partition by match_id, innings_no and ordered by over_id, ball_id to define sequence
  -- assign partnership sequence when batting pair (batsman_a_id,batsman_b_id) changes
  -- using a running sum over changes
  (1 +
    SUM(
      CASE WHEN prev.batsman_a_id IS NULL THEN 0
           WHEN (pbo.batsman_a_id = prev.batsman_a_id AND pbo.batsman_b_id = prev.batsman_b_id)
                OR (pbo.batsman_a_id = prev.batsman_b_id AND pbo.batsman_b_id = prev.batsman_a_id)
           THEN 0 ELSE 1 END
    ) OVER (PARTITION BY pbo.match_id, pbo.innings_no ORDER BY pbo.over_id, pbo.ball_id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING)
  ) AS partnership_seq,
  -- ensure deterministic low/high id ordering per requirement names
  CASE WHEN pbo.batsman_a_id <= pbo.batsman_b_id THEN pbo.batsman_a_id ELSE pbo.batsman_b_id END AS batsman_low_id,
  CASE WHEN pbo.batsman_a_id <= pbo.batsman_b_id THEN pbo.batsman_b_id ELSE pbo.batsman_a_id END AS batsman_high_id,
  -- sum runs for each batsman within the partnership sequence
  NULL AS batsman_low_runs,
  NULL AS batsman_high_runs,
  NULL AS partnership_runs
FROM partnership_ball_ownership pbo
LEFT JOIN partnership_ball_ownership prev
  ON prev.match_id = pbo.match_id
  AND prev.innings_no = pbo.innings_no
  AND prev.over_id = (
    SELECT max(p2.over_id) FROM partnership_ball_ownership p2
    WHERE p2.match_id = pbo.match_id AND p2.innings_no = pbo.innings_no
      AND (p2.over_id < pbo.over_id OR (p2.over_id = pbo.over_id AND p2.ball_id < pbo.ball_id))
  )
  AND prev.ball_id = (
    SELECT max(p3.ball_id) FROM partnership_ball_ownership p3
    WHERE p3.match_id = pbo.match_id AND p3.innings_no = pbo.innings_no
      AND (p3.over_id < pbo.over_id OR (p3.over_id = pbo.over_id AND p3.ball_id < pbo.ball_id))
  )
)
SELECT
  ppi.match_id,
  CASE
    WHEN ppi.batsman_low_runs > ppi.batsman_high_runs THEN ppi.batsman_low_id
    WHEN ppi.batsman_low_runs < ppi.batsman_high_runs THEN ppi.batsman_high_id
    WHEN ppi.batsman_low_id > ppi.batsman_high_id THEN ppi.batsman_low_id
    ELSE ppi.batsman_high_id
  END AS player1_id,
  CASE
    WHEN ppi.batsman_low_runs > ppi.batsman_high_runs THEN ppi.batsman_low_runs
    WHEN ppi.batsman_low_runs < ppi.batsman_high_runs THEN ppi.batsman_high_runs
    WHEN ppi.batsman_low_id > ppi.batsman_high_id THEN ppi.batsman_low_runs
    ELSE ppi.batsman_high_runs
  END AS player1_runs,
  CASE
    WHEN ppi.batsman_low_runs > ppi.batsman_high_runs THEN ppi.batsman_high_id
    WHEN ppi.batsman_low_runs < ppi.batsman_high_runs THEN ppi.batsman_low_id
    WHEN ppi.batsman_low_id > ppi.batsman_high_id THEN ppi.batsman_high_id
    ELSE ppi.batsman_low_id
  END AS player2_id,
  CASE
    WHEN ppi.batsman_low_runs > ppi.batsman_high_runs THEN ppi.batsman_high_runs
    WHEN ppi.batsman_low_runs < ppi.batsman_high_runs THEN ppi.batsman_low_runs
    WHEN ppi.batsman_low_id > ppi.batsman_high_id THEN ppi.batsman_high_runs
    ELSE ppi.batsman_low_runs
  END AS player2_runs,
  ppi.partnership_runs
FROM partnerships_per_innings ppi
JOIN (
  SELECT match_id, MAX(partnership_runs) AS max_partnership_runs
  FROM partnerships_per_innings
  GROUP BY match_id
) mp
  ON ppi.match_id = mp.match_id
 AND ppi.partnership_runs = mp.max_partnership_runs
ORDER BY ppi.match_id ASC, ppi.partnership_runs DESC, player1_id DESC

rows.question: Calculate the total number of wickets taken by each bowler (excluding run-outs and other dismissals not attributed to the bowler), their economy rate (total runs conceded divided by total overs bowled, considering only runs scored off the bat and ignoring any extra runs like wides and no-balls), their strike rate (average number of balls bowled per wicket taken), and their best bowling performance in a single match (the match with the most wickets taken by the bowler, formatted as "wickets-runs" where runs are the runs conceded excluding extras).
rows.pred_sql:
WITH bowler_ball_events AS (
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.bowler,
  b.team_batting,
  b.team_bowling,
  b.striker,
  bs.runs_scored,
  e.extra_type,
  e.extra_runs,
  w.player_out AS wicket_player_out,
  w.kind_out AS wicket_kind
FROM ball_by_ball b
LEFT JOIN batsman_scored bs
  ON bs.match_id = b.match_id
  AND bs.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND bs.over_id = b.over_id
  AND bs.ball_id = b.ball_id
LEFT JOIN extra_runs e
  ON e.match_id = b.match_id
  AND e.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND e.over_id = b.over_id
  AND e.ball_id = b.ball_id
LEFT JOIN wicket_taken w
  ON w.match_id = b.match_id
  AND w.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND w.over_id = b.over_id
  AND w.ball_id = b.ball_id
),
bowler_match_stats AS (
SELECT
  bbe.match_id,
  bbe.bowler AS bowler_id,
  COUNT(*) AS balls_bowled,
  SUM(CASE WHEN bbe.extra_type IS NULL OR bbe.extra_type = '' THEN IFNULL(bbe.runs_scored,0) ELSE 0 END) AS runs_conceded_off_bat,
  SUM(CASE WHEN bbe.wicket_player_out IS NOT NULL
             AND LOWER(IFNULL(bbe.wicket_kind,'')) NOT IN ('run out','retired hurt','obstructing the field')
             THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS wickets_credited
FROM
  bowler_ball_events bbe
GROUP BY
  bbe.match_id,
  bbe.bowler
),
bowler_career_aggregate AS (
SELECT
  bm.bowler_id AS bowler_id,
  SUM(bm.balls_bowled) AS balls_bowled,
  SUM(bm.runs_conceded_off_bat) AS runs_conceded_off_bat,
  SUM(bm.wickets_credited) AS total_wickets
FROM
  bowler_match_stats bm
GROUP BY
  bm.bowler_id
)
SELECT
  p.player_id AS bowler_id,
  p.player_name AS bowler_name,
  COALESCE(ca.total_wickets, 0) AS total_wickets,
  COALESCE(ca.balls_bowled, 0) AS balls_bowled,
  COALESCE(ca.runs_conceded_off_bat, 0) AS runs_conceded_off_bat,
  CASE
    WHEN ca.balls_bowled = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE (CAST(ca.runs_conceded_off_bat AS REAL) / ca.balls_bowled) * 6
  END AS economy_rate,
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(ca.total_wickets, 0) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE CAST(ca.balls_bowled AS REAL) / ca.total_wickets
  END AS strike_rate,
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(ca.total_wickets, 0) = 0 THEN '0-0'
    ELSE (best.wickets_in_match || '-' || best.runs_in_match)
  END AS best_match_performance
FROM player p
LEFT JOIN bowler_career_aggregate ca
  ON p.player_id = ca.bowler_id
LEFT JOIN (
  -- choose best match per bowler: most wickets, then fewest runs conceded, then smallest match_id
  SELECT
    bms.bowler_id,
    bms.match_id,
    bms.wickets_credited AS wickets_in_match,
    bms.runs_conceded_off_bat AS runs_in_match
  FROM (
    SELECT
      bm.*,
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
        PARTITION BY bm.bowler_id
        ORDER BY bm.wickets_credited DESC,
                 bm.runs_conceded_off_bat ASC,
                 bm.match_id ASC
      ) AS rn
    FROM bowler_match_stats bm
  ) bms
  WHERE bms.rn = 1
) best
  ON best.bowler_id = p.player_id
ORDER BY
  COALESCE(ca.total_wickets, 0) DESC,
  economy_rate ASC,
  p.player_id ASC

rows.question: List the bowlers (including their ID, first name, and last name), match number, game number, handicap score, tournament date, and location for only those bowlers who have won games with a handicap score of 190 or less at all three venues: Thunderbird Lanes, Totem Lanes, and Bolero Lanes. Only include the specific game records where they won with a handicap score of 190 or less at these three locations.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH bowler_game_scores AS (
SELECT
  BowlerID,
  MatchID,
  GameNumber,
  RawScore,
  HandiCapScore,
  WonGame
FROM Bowler_Scores
),
match_tourney_context AS (
SELECT
  TM.MatchID,
  TM.TourneyID,
  T.TourneyDate,
  T.TourneyLocation,
  TM.OddLaneTeamID,
  TM.EvenLaneTeamID
FROM Tourney_Matches TM
JOIN Tournaments T ON TM.TourneyID = T.TourneyID
),
bowlers_basic AS (
SELECT
  b.BowlerID,
  b.BowlerFirstName,
  b.BowlerLastName,
  b.TeamID,
  b.BowlerCurrentAverage,
  b.BowlerCurrentHcp
FROM Bowlers AS b
)
SELECT
  g.BowlerID,
  b.BowlerFirstName,
  b.BowlerLastName,
  g.MatchID,
  g.GameNumber,
  g.HandiCapScore,
  m.TourneyDate,
  m.TourneyLocation

JOIN match_tourney_context AS m USING (MatchID)
JOIN bowlers_basic AS b USING (BowlerID)

  AND g.HandiCapScore <= 190

    GROUP BY BowlerID
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT m2.TourneyLocation) = 3
  )
